value.rationale: The common-spoke fan is a motivated consensus/control topology interpolating hub-to-path coupling strengths. An exact all-size site count phi(2n), equality of Kalman volume across admissible single actuators, an explicit finite loss-of-rank set with positive first-order collapse, and a necessary/sufficient parameter-specific pair replacement rule together answer a natural actuator design question. These are structural quantitative boundaries, not a one-off finite sample or a known zero-forcing pair repackaged as novel.
risks: The Krylov determinant depends on units, matrix powers and coordinates and is not by itself an optimal energy measure.
General heterogeneous edge-weight extensions and other graph families remain unproved.
